summary: Implemented authorized SQLite SnapshotService with integrity-bound staged export, exact-scope fresh restore, dependency readiness, and pending-state preservation.
evidence: Public API: SnapshotService(authorizer, dependency_verifier=None).export(source, artifact, scope, credential, dependencies=()) and .restore(artifact, target, scope, credential, required_capabilities=('local',)); constructor-bound authority and dependency proof only.

Manifest snapshot/v1: source root/path/scope, captured_at, store_format, store_schema_digest, database_sha256, content_hash, completeness, dependency references/readiness, pending effect/dispatch/remote facts, and explicit no-replay/no-remote-simultaneity semantics.
Red: python -m unittest tests.local.recovery.test_snapshot_restore -v failed with ModuleNotFoundError before implementation.

Green: python -m unittest tests.local.recovery.test_snapshot_restore passed 9 tests, including authorization, trust/revocation, reviewed receipt, usage, pending/uncertain, tamper, dependency, collision, interruption, and isolation.

Preservation: python -m unittest tests.local.effects.test_local_effect_state tests.local.effects.test_external_reconciliation tests.local.usage.test_native_usage tests.local.procedures.test_procedure_contracts passed 51 tests.

Broader selector including tests.local.contracts.test_terminal_outcome ran 70 tests with one pre-existing Windows cleanup PermissionError in test_legacy_unique_binding_migrates_without_losing_history_or_ownership; isolated rerun reproduced it. This test uses sqlite3.connect as a context manager without closing the connection and is unchanged/out of scope.

Live proof gaps: STEP-15 lane 2 must bind real ROOT/operator authorization; lanes 3/4 must attest EverOS/Atlas and protected-source dependency readiness. Synthetic local proof cannot claim remote simultaneity or live-service consistency.
